title: Both identity surfaces must state all three values: the help reads as if unresolved were folded into collision (DEC-160 Ruling A)
description:
Filed from DEC-160 Ruling A, recorded as DEC-172 (4bj) on opum-doc origin/dev. Found by the quest-cli worker during QCLI-476's work and routed to opum-doc by the team lead, which ruled A and refused B.

The task-creation guide (src/application/agents/guides.ts, the refs-aware section) and the `task list --across-refs` help (src/application/command-help.ts) both describe `identity` as carrying three values -- `task`, `collision` and `unresolved` -- and both then say of the last: "an unresolved pair is reported as a collision, never assumed to be one task". The CODE and the JSON CONTRACT are unchanged and must not change: `identityOf` returns the literal `unresolved` for a 2+-state group whose states cannot be compared, and changing the code to report `collision` instead (option B) was REFUSED by DEC-160 Ruling A. What is wrong is the prose, which reads as if `unresolved` were folded into `collision` -- so a consumer following the help's own advice to read `identity` and testing `identity === "collision"` would miss a pair it should treat as unresolvable.

The precision the surfaces must carry, per opum-doc: the code returns `unresolved` when ANY state in a 2+-state group lacks a `createdAt`, not only when all of them do -- src/application/refs/across-refs.ts does `if (createdAts.has(undefined)) return "unresolved"` before it compares sizes, so a pair in which only one state is missing a `createdAt` is `unresolved`.

Both surfaces must state the three values and when each occurs, and a test must pin the DOCUMENTED value set against what the code emits, proved both ways.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The task-creation guide and the `task list --across-refs` help both state all three `identity` values -- `task`, `collision` and `unresolved` -- and when each occurs, including that `unresolved` is returned when ANY state in a 2+-state group lacks a `createdAt` (not only when all of them do), that a lone state is always `task`, and that an unresolved pair is reported as `unresolved` rather than as a collision.
A test pins the DOCUMENTED value set against the values the code emits, proved both ways: it goes red when the code's emitted set changes and when the documented set changes.
